subject: appearance of unwanted grid line and cannot reverse vertical axis

messages.author: de80823ab00b5d5b
messages.subject: appearance of unwanted grid line and cannot reverse vertical axis
parts:
Hi Group,

For the plot below, an extra grid line appears between -3.196 and
-3.3. I don't want to get rid of the grid lines, just this one. It
seems out of place, right?

Also, I would like to reverse the y-axis. I have tried setting ylim,
setting the breaks in reverse order (for both the horizontal -- before
flipping -- and the vertical axes), but this has not worked yet. Any
suggestions?

Thanks!

Juliet

myData <- read.table(textConnection("treat raw group beta lower upper
A 0.00176 High 1.09 -0.47 2.64
A 0.00176 Low -2.70 -4.70 -0.70
B 0.000636 High 0.70 -0.18 1.59
B 0.000636 Low -1.67 -2.72 -0.63
C 0.000501 High -1.42 -2.6 -0.24
C 0.000501 Low 2.09 0.46 3.73
D 0.000801 High -1.11 -2.29 0.05
D 0.000801 Low 2.27 0.64 3.92
E 0.000419 High -1.05 -2.24 0.12
E 0.000419 Low 2.54 0.89 4.19
"),header=TRUE)
closeAllConnections()

myData$lograw <- log10(myData$raw)
p <- ggplot(myData,aes(x=lograw,y=beta,colour=group,min=lower,max=upper))
p <- p + geom_pointrange(size=.7)
p <- p + scale_x_continuous(breaks=myData$lograw) + coord_flip()

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: appearance of unwanted grid line and cannot reverse vertical axis
parts:
For your plot, you might want to take control of the minor grid lines yourself:

p + scale_x_continuous(breaks=unique(myData$lograw), minor_breaks =
NA) + coord_flip()

I think the default calculation assumes evenly spaced major grid
lines, which is causing the problems.

Hadley

messages.subject: Re: appearance of unwanted grid line and cannot reverse vertical axis
parts:
Thanks!

For others, I got the reverse to work with:

scale_x_continuous(breaks=unique(myData$lograw),minor_breaks=NA,trans="reverse")
